standard.title: Consumer and financial choices
standard.description: influences on consumer choices and strategies that can be used to help make informed personal consumer and financial choices
standard.prior_knowledge: From AC9HS5K08 (Resources, needs and wants): Students understand the types of resources and the distinction between needs and wants. Students understand that scarcity requires choices to be made about resource use.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students explain the influences on consumer choices and describe strategies for making informed personal consumer and financial decisions.

nodes.label: Influences on consumer choices
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify and explain the range of factors that influence consumer purchasing decisions, including personal, social, economic, psychological, cultural, environmental and ethical factors.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify three different types of influences on consumer choices and give one example of each.
nodes.typical_width: Identify and explain the range of factors influencing consumer choices: personal preferences, social trends, economic factors (budgets, available money), psychological factors (advertising, peer pressure), and cultural, environmental, legal and ethical factors. Categorise examples of purchases using this framework.
wider: Investigate how a specific advertising or marketing strategy influences consumer behaviour — analyse an advertising campaign and assess what psychological or social levers it uses

Examine how ethical and environmental factors influence consumer choices (e.g. local vs imported products, fair trade, sustainable packaging) and evaluate whether these considerations are growing in significance
nodes.hinge_reason: Students who reduce consumer influence to a single factor (e.g. price) cannot analyse the complexity of real purchasing decisions or evaluate strategies for making better choices. The multi-factor framework is the prerequisite for understanding the range of strategies that follow.

response_modes.reason: Use a personal spending reflection (what did you buy recently? what influenced that choice?) to make the framework concrete before applying it to case study examples.

success_criteria: Students identify at least three categories of consumer influence.
Students give a specific example of each category of influence they name.

nodes.label: Selling strategies and advertising
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can compare the influence of different selling and advertising strategies on consumer choices, and explain how these strategies are designed to shape purchasing decisions.
nodes.minimum_width: Describe two selling or advertising strategies and explain how each influences consumer choices.
nodes.typical_width: Compare the influence of different advertising and selling strategies: TV and internet advertising, email promotions, peer recommendations, in-store tactics, social media influence — and explain the techniques each uses to shape consumer behaviour.
wider: Analyse a set of advertisements using media literacy tools — identifying the claims made, the techniques used, and the audience targeted
Investigate how digital advertising (including social media algorithms and targeted advertising) has changed the way businesses influence consumer choices compared with traditional advertising

response_modes.reason: Students benefit from analysing multiple advertising formats — the way advertising works differs significantly between TV, social media and in-store environments. Breadth across formats builds genuine critical consumer awareness.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Digital advertising, algorithms and targeted marketing are highly contemporary and personally relevant directions that connect economic understanding to digital literacy — this is a rich and significant extension beyond traditional advertising analysis.
success_criteria: Students describe at least two selling or advertising strategies.
Students explain the technique each strategy uses to influence consumer choice.

nodes.label: Types of financial transactions and their implications
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explain the different types of financial transactions (notes, coins, credit and debit cards, barter) and describe the advantages and disadvantages of each.
nodes.minimum_width: Name three types of financial transactions and explain one advantage and one disadvantage of each.
nodes.typical_width: Explain the range of financial transaction types: notes and coins, credit cards, debit cards, digital payments, and barter — describe the advantages and disadvantages of each type and consider how the type of transaction available may influence purchasing decisions.
wider: Investigate how digital and cashless payment systems have changed consumer behaviour, and assess the implications for record-keeping, budgeting and privacy
Explore the concept of credit and debt — when is using credit a sound financial decision and when might it lead to financial difficulty?

response_modes.reason: The advantages and disadvantages framework for transaction types requires careful analysis — avoid oversimplification (cash = bad, digital = good) by exploring real tradeoffs including access, privacy, spending behaviour and record-keeping.

success_criteria: Students name at least three types of financial transactions.
Students explain at least one advantage and one disadvantage for at least two transaction types.

nodes.label: Strategies for informed consumer and financial decisions
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can describe strategies for making informed consumer and financial decisions, and evaluate how these strategies can improve personal financial choices.
nodes.minimum_width: Describe two strategies for making informed consumer or financial decisions and explain how each leads to better decisions.
nodes.typical_width: Explain the strategies for making informed consumer and financial decisions: finding more information, comparing prices, keeping a record of money spent, saving for the future, and considering the effects on the family and community of purchase decisions.
wider: Develop a personal budget or spending plan that demonstrates application of informed decision-making strategies

Evaluate how purchasing decisions in a local supermarket have effects beyond the individual — on the family (opportunity cost), the local community (employment) and the environment (local vs imported products)

response_modes.reason: Informed financial decision-making integrates knowledge of influences (Node 1), advertising strategies (Node 2), transaction types (Node 3), and decision strategies (Node 4). Use a real or simulated purchasing decision as the integration task.

success_criteria: Students describe at least two strategies for making informed consumer or financial decisions.
Students explain how applying these strategies leads to better financial outcomes.
Students use relevant economic terms (e.g. 'consumer', 'budget', 'advertising', 'credit', 'opportunity cost') correctly.
